description.narrative: TradeMark Africa's Trade and Investment Environment Portfolio works to address the structural conditions that keep Africa's share of global trade below 3% and intra-African trade at just 15% of total trade, by operating simultaneously at three levels (continental, regional, and national) to ensure that trade agreements translate into tangible reductions in the cost and complexity of cross-border commerce. At the continental level, the Portfolio supports the AfCFTA Secretariat to develop and operationalise trade instruments, services protocols, and trade remedy frameworks; at the regional level, it works with Regional Economic Communities to facilitate intra-regional trade, domesticate continental commitments, and strengthen inter-regional cooperation, including through partnership with the EAC; and at the national level, it works with governments, corridor authorities, and trade institutions. Across all levels, the Portfolio is guided by a strategy targeting four outcomes: operationalisation of NTB frameworks and trade and investment instruments; improved market access through policy reform and services liberalisation; enhanced corridor and border management supported by data systems and regulatory transparency; and expanded regional value chains driven by export strategies and private sector development..

TradeMark Africa (TMA) accelerates economic integration across 20 sub-Saharan nations by designing regional programmes that reduce trade barriers, lower transit costs, and digitize border infrastructure. Spanning East, West, Central, Southern Africa, and the Horn, these initiatives modernise critical maritime ports and key trade corridors by replacing paper-heavy customs processes with automated digital single-window systems. By targeting green trade corridor development, supporting women and small businesses in cross-border trade, and mobilizing private capital through its commercial arm, Trade Catalyst Africa, TMA directly facilitates trade flow alignment with the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) frameworks.

provider-org.narrative: Denmark - Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Danida

receiver-org.narrative: TradeMark Africa (TMA) is a leading Aid-for-Trade organisation founded in 2010 to grow intra-African trade, increase Africa’s share in global trade, and make trade more pro-poor and sustainable. We operate on a not-for-profit basis, funded by a strong coalition of development partners including Canada, Denmark, the European Union, Finland, France, the Gates Foundation, Ireland, the Mastercard Foundation, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden and the United Kingdom. TMA works closely with regional and continental institutions, national governments, the private sector, and civil society to unlock trade and investment opportunities across the continent.

comment.narrative: 6.6 million exchanges enabled on the EAC Single Customs Territory Central Platform, enabling real-time customs and port data exchange; more than 800,000 transactions processed since it's rollout.
